drivingQuestion: Which cuts of the windpipe are valid — inside the rings other than the large one, above the large ring, and where diversion or a perforation interrupts the cut?
outcomeNote: Two explicit halakhic conclusions are reached — that slaughter from the incline of the thyroid cartilage downward is valid (19a.1) and that the halakha follows R׳ Ḥanina ben Antigonus on a diverted cut (19a.7) — while the closing dispute over a perforation met midway ends with R׳ Yoḥanan rejecting R׳ Elazar's analogy and Rava endorsing that rejection; the earlier dilemma about the sense of פגע (18b.11) is never answered in its own terms.

segments.he: גְּמָ׳ רַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, וְאַף רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה לֹא אָמַר אֶלָּא בְּטַבַּעַת הַגְּדוֹלָה, הוֹאִיל וּמַקֶּפֶת אֶת כׇּל הַקָּנֶה, אֲבָל בִּשְׁאָר טַבָּעוֹת – לֹא.
segments.en: «GEMARA:» It is «Rav and Shmuel who both say:» The «halakha» is «in accordance with» the opinion of «Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda. And even Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, says» his statement «only with regard to the large» upper «ring, since it encircles the entire windpipe, but with regard to the rest of the rings,» which are incomplete and where a strip of flesh connects their edges, he did «not» state his halakha. Therefore, his slaughter is not valid, as he is required to slaughter in the space between those rings and not in the rings themselves.

segments.he: וּבִשְׁאָר טַבָּעוֹת לֹא? וְהָתַנְיָא: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר:
segments.en: The Gemara objects: «And with regard to the rest of the rings,» Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, did «not» state his halakha; «but isn’t it taught» in a baraita that «Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, says:»

segments.he: הַשּׁוֹחֵט בִּשְׁאָר טַבָּעוֹת, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין מַקִּיפוֹת אֶת כׇּל הַקָּנֶה, הוֹאִיל וּמַקִּיפוֹת אֶת רוֹב הַקָּנֶה – שְׁחִיטָתוֹ כְּשֵׁרָה, וּמוּגְרֶמֶת פְּסוּלָה. הֵעִיד רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן אַנְטִיגְנוֹס עַל מוּגְרֶמֶת שֶׁהִיא כְּשֵׁרָה.
segments.en: With regard to «one who slaughters» from «within the rest of the rings, even though they do not encircle the entire windpipe, since they encircle the majority of the windpipe his slaughter is valid.» The baraita adds: «And» in a case where the knife «is diverted» from the place of slaughter above the ring, the slaughter is «not valid. Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigonus testified about» a case where the knife «is diverted» from the area of slaughter above the ring «that» in such a case the slaughter is «valid.» Contrary to that which Rav and Shmuel said with regard to the opinion of Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, he holds that slaughter from within the other rings is valid.

segments.he: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר יְהוּדָה תַּרְתֵּי קָאָמַר. רַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל סָבְרִי כְּוָותֵיהּ בַּחֲדָא, וּפְלִיגִי עֲלֵיהּ בַּחֲדָא.
segments.en: «Rav Yosef said: Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda is saying two» statements; «Rav and Shmuel hold in accordance with his» opinion «with regard to one» matter, that if one cuts a majority of the windpipe within the large ring the slaughter is valid, «and disagree with him with regard to one» matter, as in their opinion if one cuts the windpipe within the other rings, the slaughter is not valid.

segments.he: וְהָא ״לֹא אָמַר״ קָאָמְרִי? הָכִי קָאָמַר: הֲלָכָה כְּמוֹתוֹ בְּטַבַּעַת הַגְּדוֹלָה, וְאֵין הֲלָכָה כְּמוֹתוֹ בִּשְׁאָר טַבָּעוֹת.
segments.en: The Gemara objects: «But didn’t» Rav and Shmuel «say:» And even Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, «said» his statement «only» with regard to the large upper ring and not with regard to the other rings, indicating that in their opinion, this is the opinion of Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda? The Gemara explains that «this» is what Rav and Shmuel are «saying:» The «halakha» is «in accordance with» the opinion of Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, «with regard to» cutting the majority of the windpipe within «the large ring, and» the «halakha» is «not in accordance with his» opinion «with regard to» the «other rings» that since they encircle a majority of the windpipe, one may slaughter within them as well.

segments.he: כִּי סְלֵיק רַבִּי זֵירָא, אֲכַל מוּגְרֶמֶת דְּרַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל. אָמְרִי לֵיהּ: לָאו מֵאַתְרֵיהּ דְּרַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל אַתְּ? אֲמַר לְהוּ: מַאן אַמְרַהּ? יוֹסֵף בַּר חִיָּיא! יוֹסֵף בַּר חִיָּיא מִכּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא גְּמִיר.
segments.en: «When Rabbi Zeira ascended» from Babylonia to Eretz Yisrael, «he ate» meat from an animal during whose slaughter the knife was «diverted» from the place of slaughter, with regard to «which Rav and Shmuel» ruled that the slaughter is not valid, and in Eretz Yisrael the ruling was that the slaughter is valid. The Torah scholars in Eretz Yisrael «said to» Rabbi Zeira: «Aren’t you from» Babylonia, «the place where Rav and Shmuel» are the halakhic authorities? You should follow their ruling. Rabbi Zeira «said to them: Who said» this halakha citing Rav and Shmuel? It was «Yosef bar Ḥiyya,» referring to Rav Yosef. «Yosef bar Ḥiyya learns from everyone,» even from students of Rav and Shmuel who misquote their statements.

segments.he: שְׁמַע רַב יוֹסֵף, אִיקְּפַד, אֲמַר: אֲנָא מִכּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא גְּמִירְנָא? אֲנָא מֵרַב יְהוּדָה גְּמִירְנָא, דַּאֲפִילּוּ סְפֵיקֵי דְּגַבְרֵי גָּרֵיס. דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא, סָפֵק מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב, סָפֵק מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל: שְׁלֹשָׁה מַתִּירִין אֶת הַבְּכוֹר בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁאֵין מוּמְחֶה.
segments.en: «Rav Yosef heard» the comment of Rabbi Zeira and «was angry. He said:» Do «I learn from everyone? I learn from Rav Yehuda,» who is so meticulous in citing the statements of Rav and Shmuel «that he cites even uncertainties» with regard to attribution of statements «to the men» who said them. «As Rav Yehuda says» that «Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba says,» and it is «uncertain» whether it is «in the name of Rav» and «uncertain» whether it is «in the name of Shmuel:» A tribunal of «three permits» slaughter of a blemished «firstborn» animal outside of the Temple «in a place where there is no expert» Sage to consult.

segments.he: וְרַבִּי זֵירָא, לֵית לֵיהּ נוֹתְנִין עָלָיו חוּמְרֵי הַמָּקוֹם שֶׁיָּצָא מִשָּׁם וְחוּמְרֵי הַמָּקוֹם שֶׁהָלַךְ לְשָׁם?
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «And does Rabbi Zeira not accept» the principle that when a person travels from place to place, the Sages «impose upon him the stringencies of the place from which he emerged and the stringencies of the place to which he went?»

segments.he: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הָנֵי מִילֵּי מִבָּבֶל לְבָבֶל, וּמֵאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל לְאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל, אִי נָמֵי מֵאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל לְבָבֶל, אֲבָל מִבָּבֶל לְאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל, כֵּיוָן דַּאֲנַן כַּיְיפִינַן לְהוּ – עָבְדִינַן כְּוָותַיְיהוּ.
segments.en: «Abaye said: That statement» applies when one travels «from» one place in «Babylonia to» another place in «Babylonia, or from» one place in «Eretz Yisrael to» another place in «Eretz Yisrael,» or «alternatively,» when one descends «from Eretz Yisrael to Babylonia. But» when one ascends «from Babylonia to Eretz Yisrael,» this principle does not apply. «Since we,» the residents of Babylonia, «are subordinate to them» in terms of halakha, «we act in accordance with their» custom.

segments.he: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא מִבָּבֶל לְאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל, הָנֵי מִילֵּי הֵיכָא דְּדַעְתּוֹ לַחֲזוֹר, רַבִּי זֵירָא אֵין דַּעְתּוֹ לַחֲזוֹר הֲוָה.
segments.en: «Rav Ashi said: Even» if «you say» that when one travels «from Babylonia to Eretz Yisrael,» he is required to act stringently in accordance with the custom of the place from which he emerged, «that statement» applies only in a case «where his intent is to return. Rabbi Zeira was not» one «whose intent was to return.» Therefore, he was not obligated to observe the Babylonian stringencies.

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי לְרַב יוֹסֵף: וְהָא רַבָּנַן דַּאֲתוֹ מִמָּחוֹזָא אָמְרִי, אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן: מוּגְרֶמֶת כְּשֵׁרָה! אֲמַר לֵיהּ: נַהֲרָא נַהֲרָא וּפְשָׁטֵיהּ.
segments.en: «Abaye said to Rav Yosef: But didn’t the Sages who came from Meḥoza say» that «Rabbi Zeira says in the name of Rav Naḥman:» In a case where the knife «is diverted» from the place of slaughter above the ring, the slaughter is «valid?» Rav Yosef «said to him: Each river and its» unique «course,» i.e., each place follows its custom, and in Meḥoza the custom was not in accordance with the opinion of Rav and Shmuel.

segments.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ אַכְשַׁר בְּחוּדָּא דְּכוֹבָעָא, קָרֵי עֲלֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: גִּיסָא גִּיסָא, אָמַר רַב פַּפִּי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא: פְּגַע בְּחִיטֵּי – טְרֵפָה.
segments.en: The Gemara relates that «Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish deemed» the slaughter «valid» in a case where one cut the windpipe «at the tip of the thyroid cartilage» that is above the large ring. «Rabbi Yoḥanan proclaimed about» Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish: He «greatly exaggerated» the limits of valid slaughter. «Rav Pappi said in the name of Rava:» If one cut the windpipe and «encountered the arytenoid cartilage» that is adjacent to the upper ring in the direction of the jaw and covered by the tip of the thyroid cartilage, the animal is «a tereifa,» i.e., forbidden. Since the arytenoid cartilage is outside the area of slaughter, the slaughter is invalid.

segments.he: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: פָּגַע וְנָגַע בָּהֶן, דִּכְתִיב ״וַיִּפְגַּע בּוֹ וַיָּמֹת״, אוֹ דִלְמָא פָּגַע וְלֹא נָגַע, כְּדִכְתִיב ״וַיִּפְגְּעוּ בוֹ מַלְאֲכֵי אֱלֹהִים״?
segments.en: «A dilemma was raised before» the Sages: Does encountered mean «encountered and touched it, as it is written: “And he encountered him and he died”» (I Kings 2:25); «or perhaps» it means «encountered but did not touch, like that which is written: “And the angels of God encountered him”» (Genesis 32:2)?

segments.he: אִיתְּמַר, אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא: שַׁיַּיר בְּחִיטֵּי – כְּשֵׁרָה. אָמַר רַב אַמֵּימָר בַּר מָר יָנוֹקָא: הֲוָה קָאֵימְנָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אַוְיָא, וְאָמַר לִי: שַׁיַּיר בְּחִיטֵּי – כְּשֵׁרָה. אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי: אֲמַר לִי רַב שֶׁמֶן מִסּוּבְרָא, אִיקְּלַע מָר זוּטְרָא לְאַתְרִין וּדְרַשׁ: שַׁיַּיר בְּחִיטֵּי – כְּשֵׁרָה. מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: פְּגַע בְּחִיטֵּי – כְּשֵׁרָה, שַׁיַּיר בְּחִיטֵּי – טְרֵפָה.
segments.en: «It was stated» that «Rav Pappa said in the name of Rava:» If «one left» part «of the arytenoid cartilage,» i.e., if he cut it in the middle, the slaughter is «valid. Rav Ameimar bar Mar Yenuka said: I was standing before Rabbi Ḥiyya, son of Rav Avya, and he said to me:» If «one left» part «of the arytenoid cartilage,» the slaughter is «valid. Ravina said to Rav Ashi: Rav Shemen of Suvara said to me» that «Mar Zutra happened» to come «to our place and taught:» If «one left» part «of the arytenoid cartilage,» the slaughter is «valid. Mar bar Rav Ashi said:» If «one encountered the arytenoid cartilage,» the slaughter is «valid.» If «one left» part «of the arytenoid cartilage,» the animal is «a tereifa.»

segments.he: וְהִלְכְתָא מִשִּׁיפּוּי כּוֹבַע וּלְמַטָּה – כְּשֵׁרָה, וְהַיְינוּ דְּשַׁיַּיר בְּחִיטֵּי.
segments.en: The Gemara concludes: «And the halakha» is: If one slaughters «from the incline of the thyroid cartilage and below» in the direction of the windpipe, the slaughter is «valid, and that is in» accordance with the opinion «that one who left» part «of the arytenoid cartilage» has still performed a valid slaughter, as the arytenoids cartilage extends beyond this point.

segments.he: רַב נַחְמָן אַכְשַׁר מִשִּׁיפּוּי כּוֹבַע וּלְמַטָּה, אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב חָנָן בַּר רַב קַטִּינָא לְרַב נַחְמָן: כְּמַאן? לָא כְּרַבָּנַן וְלָא כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
segments.en: The Gemara relates that «Rav Naḥman deemed» the slaughter «valid» in a case where one slaughtered «from the incline of the thyroid cartilage and below. Rav Ḥanan bar Rav Ketina said to Rav Naḥman: In accordance with whose» opinion is that ruling? It is «neither in accordance with» the opinion of «the Rabbis nor in accordance with» the opinion of «Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda,» who both hold that if one cuts the windpipe above the large upper ring, the cricoid cartilage, the slaughter is not valid.

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲנָא לָא חִילָק יָדַעְנָא וְלָא בִּילָק יָדַעְנָא, אֲנָא שְׁמַעְתָּא יָדַעְנָא, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר זַבְדָּא אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא, וְאָמְרִי לָהּ אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אִידִי אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: מִשִּׁיפּוּי כּוֹבַע וּלְמַטָּה כְּשֵׁרָה.
segments.en: Rav Naḥman «said to him: Neither do I know Ḥillek nor do I know Billek,» i.e., I know the reason neither for this one’s opinion nor for that one’s opinion. «I know the halakha, as Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba says» that «Rabbi Yoḥanan says, and some say» that «Rabbi Abba bar Zavda says» that «Rabbi Ḥanina says, and some say» that «Rabbi Ya’akov bar Idi says» that «Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi says: From the incline of the thyroid cartilage and below,» the slaughter is «valid.»

segments.he: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: מוּגְרֶמֶת דְּרַבָּנַן כְּשֵׁרָה לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
segments.en: § The Gemara returns to analyzing the baraita (18b): In a case where the knife is diverted from the place of slaughter above the ring, the slaughter is not valid. Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigonus testified about a case where the knife is diverted from the place of slaughter above the ring that the slaughter is valid. «And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi says:» With regard to a case where the knife was «diverted» according to the opinion «of the Rabbis» cited in the mishna, the slaughter is «valid» according «to» the opinion of «Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda,» who ruled that the slaughter is valid when the majority of the windpipe was cut within the large, upper ring.

segments.he: וּדְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, כְּשֵׁרָה לְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן אַנְטִיגְנוֹס.
segments.en: «And» with regard to a case where the knife was «diverted» according to the opinion «of Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda,» it is «valid» according «to» the opinion of «Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigonus,» who ruled that even if a majority of the windpipe was cut outside the large upper ring, the slaughter is valid.

segments.he: פְּשִׁיטָא! מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן אַנְטִיגְנוֹס אַדְּרַבָּנַן קָאֵי, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן.
segments.en: The Gemara objects: That is «obvious.» The Gemara explains: «Lest you say» that the statement of «Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigonus,» who ruled that in a case where the knife is diverted from the place of slaughter above the ring it is valid, «addresses» the statement «of the Rabbis» and he agrees with the opinion of Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, that the slaughter is not valid when the majority of the windpipe was cut above the large upper ring, therefore, Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi «teaches us» that this is not the case.

segments.he: וְאֵימָא הָכִי נָמֵי? אִם כֵּן, ״הֵעִיד עָלֶיהָ״ מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ. וְהִלְכְתָא כְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן אַנְטִיגְנוֹס, דְּקָאֵי רַב נַחְמָן כְּוָותֵיהּ.
segments.en: The Gemara objects: «And say it is indeed so» that Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigonus agrees with Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda. The Gemara responds: «If so,» the formulation of the baraita «should have» been: Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigonus «testified about it.» Since the opinion of Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigonus was introduced merely with the term: Testified, apparently he disagrees with all of the other opinions. The Gemara concludes: «And the halakha is in accordance with» the opinion of «Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigonus, as Rav Naḥman holds in accordance with his» opinion.

segments.he: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב אַסִּי: מַחְלוֹקֶת בְּשֶׁשָּׁחַט שְׁנֵי שְׁלִישׁ וְהִגְרִים שְׁלִישׁ, דְּרַבָּנַן סָבְרִי: כּוּלַּהּ שְׁחִיטָה בָּעֵינַן בְּטַבַּעַת גְּדוֹלָה, וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר: רוּבּוֹ כְּכוּלּוֹ.
segments.en: § The mishna cited a dispute between the Rabbis, who hold that in a case where one slaughtered within the large upper ring and did not leave a thread breadth over the entire surface of the ring, the slaughter is not valid, and Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, who hold that even if one left a thread breadth over a majority of the surface of the ring, the slaughter is valid. Apropos to that, «Rav Huna said» that «Rav Asi says:» The «dispute» is only «in» a case «where one cut two-thirds» of the windpipe within the ring «and» then «diverted» the knife upward toward the head of the animal and cut the remaining «one-third, as the Rabbis hold» that «we require the entire slaughter» to be performed «within the large ring, and Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, holds:» The halakhic status of «its majority is like» that of «its entirety.»

segments.he: אֲבָל הִגְרִים שְׁלִישׁ, וְשָׁחַט שְׁנֵי שְׁלִישׁ – דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל פְּסוּלָה, דְּכִי נָפְקָא חִיּוּתָא בָּעֵינַן רוּבָּא בִּשְׁחִיטָה, וְלֵיכָּא.
segments.en: «But» if «one diverted» the knife upward toward the head of the animal, cut «one-third» of the windpipe, «and» then «cut two-thirds» within the ring, «everyone agrees» that the slaughter is «not valid, as when the life left» the animal, i.e., when the majority of the windpipe was cut, «we require» that the entire «majority» be cut «by means of slaughter, and that is not» so in this case.

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב חִסְדָּא: אַדְּרַבָּה, לֵימָא מָר אִיפְּכָא: מַחְלוֹקֶת כְּשֶׁהִגְרִים שְׁלִישׁ, וְשָׁחַט שְׁנֵי שְׁלִישׁ, דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר מִידֵּי דְּהָוֵה אַחֲצִי קָנֶה פָּגוּם.
segments.en: «Rav Ḥisda said to» Rav Huna: «On the contrary, let the Master say the opposite.» The «dispute» is only «in» a case «when one diverted» the knife upward toward the head of the animal, cut «one-third» of the windpipe, «and» then «cut two-thirds» within the ring, «as Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, holds» that the slaughter is valid «just as it is» in the case «where half the windpipe is deficient.» In that case, once the slaughterer cuts any additional part of the windpipe, the slaughter is valid because the cut that rendered a majority of the windpipe slaughtered was performed properly. So too in this case, since the cut of the second third was performed properly, the slaughter is valid.

segments.he: וְרַבָּנַן, הָתָם מָקוֹם שְׁחִיטָה, הָכָא לָאו מְקוֹם שְׁחִיטָה.
segments.en: «And the Rabbis» hold that «there,» in the case of the deficient windpipe, the deficiency was in «the place of» proper «slaughter,» and therefore most of the life of the animal left in the proper place. «Here,» the first third was cut while the knife was diverted, and therefore most of the life of the animal did «not» leave in «the place of» proper «slaughter.»

segments.he: אֲבָל שָׁחַט שְׁנֵי שְׁלִישׁ, וְהִגְרִים שְׁלִישׁ – דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל כְּשֵׁרָה, דְּהָא תְּנַן: רוּבּוֹ שֶׁל אֶחָד כָּמוֹהוּ.
segments.en: «But» in a case where «one cut two-thirds» of the windpipe within the ring «and» then «diverted» the knife and cut the remaining «one-third, everyone agrees» that the slaughter is «valid, as didn’t we learn» in a mishna (27a): The halakhic status of the slaughter of the «majority of one» siman, the windpipe or the gullet, «is like» that of the slaughter of the entire siman «itself?»

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יוֹסֵף: מַאן נֵימָא לַן דְּהָהוּא רוּבָּא דְּהָתָם לָאו רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה קָתָנֵי לַהּ? דִּלְמָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה קָתָנֵי לַהּ!
segments.en: «Rav Yosef said to» Rav Ḥisda: «Who will say to us that» with regard to the mishna «there» concerning «the majority of» one siman, «Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, did not teach it? Perhaps Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, taught it,» and the Rabbis disagree.

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: אַטּוּ כֹּל רוּבֵּי דְּעָלְמָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה קָתָנֵי לְהוּ? אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲנָא רוּבָּא דִּשְׁחִיטָה קָאָמֵינָא, דִּשְׁמַעְנָא לְהוּ דִּפְלִיגִי.
segments.en: «Abaye said to» Rav Yosef: «Is that to say» that with regard to «all» principles that address «majorities in general, Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, taught them?» Rav Yosef «said to him: I am speaking of the» principle of «majority with regard to slaughter, as we heard that» the Rabbis «disagree» with him.

segments.he: לִישָּׁנָא אַחֲרִינָא אָמְרִי לַהּ, אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב אַסִּי: מַחְלוֹקֶת שֶׁהִגְרִים שְׁלִישׁ וְשָׁחַט שְׁנֵי שְׁלִישׁ, דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר: מִידֵּי דְּהָוֵה אַחֲצִי קָנֶה פָּגוּם, וְרַבָּנַן – הָתָם מְקוֹם שְׁחִיטָה, הָכָא לָאו מְקוֹם שְׁחִיטָה.
segments.en: «Some say» that there is «an alternative version» of this discussion: «Rav Huna said» that «Rav Asi says:» The «dispute» is only in a case «where one diverted» the knife upward toward the head of the animal, cut «one-third» of the windpipe, «and» then «cut two-thirds» within the ring, «as Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, holds» that the slaughter is valid «just as it is» in the case «where half the windpipe is deficient, and the Rabbis» hold that «there,» in the case of the deficient windpipe, the deficiency was in «the place of» proper «slaughter,» but «here,» most of the life of the animal did «not» leave in «the place of» proper «slaughter.»

segments.he: אֲבָל שָׁחַט שְׁנֵי שְׁלִישׁ, וְהִגְרִים שְׁלִישׁ – דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל כְּשֵׁרָה, דְּהָא תְּנַן: רוּבּוֹ שֶׁל אֶחָד כָּמוֹהוּ.
segments.en: «But» in a case where «one cut two-thirds» of the windpipe within the ring «and» then «diverted» the knife and cut the remaining «one-third, everyone agrees» that the slaughter is «valid, as didn’t we learn» in a mishna (27a): The halakhic status of the slaughter of the «majority of one» siman, the windpipe or the gullet, «is like» that of the slaughter of the entire siman «itself?»

segments.he: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב חִסְדָּא: מַאן לֵימָא לַן דְּהָהוּא רוּבָּא דְּהָתָם לָאו רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה קָתָנֵי לַהּ? דִּלְמָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה קָתָנֵי לַהּ! אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יוֹסֵף: אַטּוּ כֹּל רוּבֵּי דְּעָלְמָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה קָתָנֵי לְהוּ? אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲנָא רוּבָּא דִּשְׁחִיטָה קָאָמֵינָא, דִּשְׁמַעְנָא לְהוּ דִּפְלִיגִי.
segments.en: «Rav Ḥisda objects to this: Who will say to us that» with regard to the mishna «there» concerning «the majority of» one siman, «Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, did not teach it? Perhaps Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, taught it,» and the Rabbis disagree. «Rav Yosef said to» Rav Ḥisda: «Is that to say» that with regard to «all» principles that address «majorities in general, Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, taught them?» Rav Ḥisda «said to him: I am speaking of the» principle of «majority with regard to slaughter, as we heard that» the Rabbis «disagree» with him.

segments.he: הִגְרִים שְׁלִישׁ, וְשָׁחַט שְׁלִישׁ, וְהִגְרִים שְׁלִישׁ – רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב: כְּשֵׁרָה, רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: טְרֵפָה. רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב: כְּשֵׁרָה – כִּי נָפְקָא חִיּוּתָא בִּשְׁחִיטָה קָא נָפְקָא. רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: טְרֵפָה – בָּעֵינַן רוּבָּא בִּשְׁחִיטָה וְלֵיכָּא.
segments.en: § If «one diverted» the knife and cut «one-third» of the windpipe, «and» then «cut one-third» properly, «and» then «diverted» and cut the final «one-third, Rav Huna» says that «Rav says:» The slaughter is «valid. Rav Yehuda» says that «Rav says:» The animal is «a tereifa,» i.e., forbidden. «Rav Huna» says that «Rav says:» The slaughter is «valid,» as «when the life left» the animal, it was «in» the course of a valid «slaughter» that «it left. Rav Yehuda» says that «Rav says:» The animal is «a tereifa, as we require a majority» of the windpipe to be cut «with» valid «slaughter,and» that «is not» the case.

segments.he: שָׁחַט שְׁלִישׁ, וְהִגְרִים שְׁלִישׁ, וְשָׁחַט שְׁלִישׁ – רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: כְּשֵׁרָה. אֲתוֹ שַׁיְילוּהּ לְרַב הוּנָא, אֲמַר לְהוּ: טְרֵפָה. שְׁמַע רַב יְהוּדָה אִיקְּפַד, אֲמַר: טָרֵיפְנָא (ומכשר) [מַכְשַׁר], (ומכשרנא) [מַכְשַׁרְנָא] טָרֵיף! אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: שַׁפִּיר קָא מִיקְּפַד, חֲדָא – אִיהוּ שְׁמִיעַ לֵיהּ מִינֵּיהּ דְּרַב, וַאֲנָא לָא שְׁמִיעַ לִי, וְעוֹד – הָאִיכָּא רוּבָּא בִּשְׁחִיטָה.
segments.en: If «one cut one-third» of the windpipe properly, «and» then «diverted» the knife and cut «one-third, and» then «cut» the final «one-third» of the windpipe properly, «Rav Yehuda» says that «Rav said:» The slaughter is «valid.» When the Sages «came and asked Rav Huna, he said to them:» It is «a tereifa. Rav Yehuda heard» the ruling of Rav Huna, and «he was angry. He said: I deem» it «a tereifa and he deems» the slaughter «valid, and I deem» the slaughter «valid» and «he deems» it «a tereifa. Rav Huna said:» It is «proper» that «he was angry. One» reason is that «he heard» it «from Rav and I did not hear» it from Rav; «and furthermore, isn’t there the majority» of the siman that was cut «with» valid «slaughter?»

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב חִסְדָּא: לָא תֶּהְדַּר בָּךְ,
segments.en: «Rav Ḥisda said to» Rav Huna: «Do not retract» your statement,

segments.he: דְּאִם כֵּן, מַפְסְדַתְּ לַהּ לְקַמַּיְיתָא. הָתָם מַאי טַעְמָא קָא מַכְשְׁרַתְּ? דְּכִי נָפְקָא חִיּוּתָא – בְּהֶכְשֵׁירַהּ קָא נָפְקָא. הָכָא נָמֵי, כִּי נָפְקָא חִיּוּתָא – בְּהַגְרָמָה קָא נָפְקָא.
segments.en: «as, if» you retract your statement, «you repudiate the first» ruling that you stated with regard to a case where one diverted the knife and cut one-third of the windpipe, and then cut one-third properly, and then diverted and cut the final one-third. «There, what is the reason» that «you deemed» the slaughter «valid?» The reason is «that when life left» the animal with the cutting of the second third of the windpipe, «it left» the animal «in» the course of «valid» slaughter. Based on that reasoning, «here too, when life left» the animal with the cutting of the second third of the windpipe, «it left» the animal «in» the course of «diverting» the knife, and the slaughter is invalid.

segments.he: אִיקְּלַע רַב נַחְמָן לְסוּרָא, בְּעוֹ מִינֵּיהּ: שָׁחַט שְׁלִישׁ וְהִגְרִים שְׁלִישׁ וְשָׁחַט שְׁלִישׁ, מַהוּ? אֲמַר לְהוּ: לָאו הַיְינוּ דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי: שְׁחִיטָה הָעֲשׂוּיָה כְּמַסְרֵק כְּשֵׁרָה.
segments.en: «Rav Naḥman happened» to come «to Sura,» where «they asked him:» If «one cut one-third» of the windpipe properly, «and» then «diverted» the knife and cut «one-third, and» then «cut» the final «one-third» of the windpipe properly, «what is» the halakha? «He said to them: Isn’t that» the halakha stated by «Rabbi Elazar bar Minyumi, as Rabbi Elazar bar Minyumi says: Slaughter that is performed like» the teeth of «a comb,» which are jagged, is «valid.»

segments.he: וְדִלְמָא בִּמְקוֹם שְׁחִיטָה! בִּמְקוֹם שְׁחִיטָה מַאי לְמֵימְרָא? מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: בָּעֵינַן שְׁחִיטָה מְפוֹרַעַת וְלֵיכָּא, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן.
segments.en: The Gemara objects: «And perhaps» Rabbi Elazar bar Minyumi stated his halakha only when the slaughter goes up and down «within» the proper «place of slaughter.» The Gemara asks in response: «Within» the proper «place of slaughter, what» is the purpose «of stating» it? Clearly the slaughter is valid in that case. The Gemara explains: «Lest you say» that «we require slaughter» that is «clear» and straight, «and» slaughter that is jagged «is not» straight, therefore, Rabbi Elazar bar Minyumi «teaches us» that nevertheless, the slaughter is valid.
The Gemara cites «a mnemonic» for the order of the Sages in the following discussion: «Beit» for Rabbi Abba; «kaf» for Rav Kahana; «dalet» for Rav Yehuda.

segments.he: יְתֵיב רַבִּי אַבָּא אֲחוֹרֵיהּ דְּרַב כָּהֲנָא, וְיָתֵיב רַב כָּהֲנָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה, וְיָתֵיב וְקָאָמַר: שָׁחַט שְׁלִישׁ וְהִגְרִים שְׁלִישׁ וְשָׁחַט שְׁלִישׁ, מַהוּ? אֲמַר לֵיהּ: שְׁחִיטָתוֹ כְּשֵׁרָה.
segments.en: «Rabbi Abba sat behind Rav Kahana and Rav Kahana sat before Rav Yehuda, and he sat and said» to Rav Yehuda: If «one cut one-third» of the windpipe properly, «and» then «diverted» the knife and cut «one-third, and» then «cut» the final «one-third» of the windpipe properly, «what is» the halakha? Rav Yehuda «said to» Rav Kahana: «His slaughter is valid.»

segments.he: הִגְרִים שְׁלִישׁ וְשָׁחַט שְׁלִישׁ וְהִגְרִים שְׁלִישׁ, מַהוּ? אֲמַר לֵיהּ: שְׁחִיטָתוֹ פְּסוּלָה.
segments.en: Rav Kahana then asked: If «one diverted» the knife and cut «one-third» of the windpipe, «and» then «cut one-third» properly, «and» then «diverted» and cut the final «one-third, what is» the halakha? Rav Yehuda «said to» him: «His slaughter is not valid.»

segments.he: שָׁחַט בִּמְקוֹם נֶקֶב, מַהוּ? אֲמַר לֵיהּ: שְׁחִיטָתוֹ כְּשֵׁרָה.
segments.en: Rav Kahana then asked: If «one cut in a place» where there was «a perforation» in the front of the windpipe and continued cutting, «what is» the halakha? Rav Yehuda «said to» him: «His slaughter is valid.»

segments.he: שָׁחַט וּפָגַע בּוֹ נֶקֶב, מַהוּ? אֲמַר לֵיהּ: שְׁחִיטָתוֹ פְּסוּלָה.
segments.en: Rav Kahana further asked: If «one cut» the windpipe «and» after cutting half the windpipe «encountered a perforation,» after which point a majority of the windpipe had been cut, «what is» the halakha? Rav Yehuda «said to» him: «His slaughter is not valid.»

segments.he: אֲזַל רַבִּי אַבָּא, אַמְרַהּ קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, אֲזַל רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, אַמְרַהּ קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מַאי שְׁנָא?
segments.en: «Rabbi Abba went» to Eretz Yisrael and «stated» these halakhot «in the presence of Rabbi Elazar,» and «Rabbi Elazar went» and «stated» these halakhot «in the presence of Rabbi Yoḥanan.» Rabbi Yoḥanan «said to him: What is different» about a case where one cut in a place where there was a perforation relative to a case where he encountered a perforation in the middle of the slaughter?

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: שָׁחַט בִּמְקוֹם נֶקֶב, נַעֲשָׂה כְּמִי שֶׁשָּׁחַט גּוֹי וְגָמַר יִשְׂרָאֵל. שָׁחַט וּפָגַע בּוֹ נֶקֶב, נַעֲשָׂה כְּמִי שֶׁשָּׁחַט יִשְׂרָאֵל וְגָמַר גּוֹי. קָרֵי עֲלֵיהּ: ״גּוֹי גּוֹי״.
segments.en: Rabbi Elazar «said to him:» In a case where «one cut in a place» where there was «a perforation, it becomes like» an animal «that a gentile» began to «slaughter and a Jew completed» its slaughter, in which case the slaughter is valid. In a case where «one cut» the windpipe «and encountered a perforation, it becomes like» an animal «that a Jew» began to «slaughter and a gentile completed» its slaughter, in which case the slaughter is not valid. Rabbi Yoḥanan mockingly «proclaimed about him: Gentile, gentile,» i.e., you merely repeat something about gentiles. Rabbi Yoḥanan did not accept the distinction.

segments.he: אָמַר רָבָא: שַׁפִּיר קָרֵי עֲלֵיהּ ״גּוֹי גּוֹי״, בִּשְׁלָמָא הָתָם מִדַּהֲוָה לֵיהּ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל לְמִשְׁחַט רוּבָּא וְלָא שְׁחַט, כִּי נָפְקָא חִיּוּתָא – בִּידָא דְּגוֹי קָא נָפְקָא, אֶלָּא הָכָא מִכְּדֵי מִשְׁחָט שָׁחֵיט, מָה לִי בִּמְקוֹם נֶקֶב, מָה לִי פָּגַע בּוֹ נֶקֶב?
segments.en: «Rava said:» Rabbi Yoḥanan did «well» when he «proclaimed about him: Gentile, gentile. Granted, there,» in the case where the gentile completed the slaughter, «since a Jew was» supposed «to cut a majority» of the windpipe «and he did not cut» it, «when life left» the animal «it left by the hand of a gentile. But here, after all, he» was the one who «slaughtered» the entire animal, and the animal was not a tereifa until this point, and so «what» difference is there «to me» if one began to cut «in a place» where there was «a perforation» and «what» difference is there «to me» if he «encountered a perforation?»

moves.summary: Rav and Shmuel rule like R׳ Yosei b׳R׳ Yehuda of the mishna, but only for the large upper ring.
moves.about: whether the halakha follows R׳ Yosei b׳R׳ Yehuda that cutting the majority of a ring counts as cutting all of it

moves.summary: A baraita is raised against their restriction of R׳ Yosei to the large ring.
moves.about: whether R׳ Yosei b׳R׳ Yehuda really withheld his ruling from the rings other than the large one

moves.summary: The baraita: R׳ Yosei validates the other rings, holds a diverted cut invalid, and R׳ Ḥanina ben Antigonus testifies it is valid.
moves.about: the baraita in which R׳ Yosei b׳R׳ Yehuda validates slaughter within the other rings

moves.cueHe: אמר רב יוסף: רבי יוסי בר יהודה תרתי קאמר
moves.summary: R׳ Yosei made two statements; Rav and Shmuel accept one and reject the other.
moves.about: how Rav and Shmuel can rule like R׳ Yosei b׳R׳ Yehuda and yet exclude the other rings

moves.summary: Their wording ׳he did not say׳ ascribes the restriction to R׳ Yosei, not to their own dissent.
moves.about: Rav and Shmuel's wording ׳he did not say׳ ascribes the restriction to R׳ Yosei b׳R׳ Yehuda himself, not to their own dissent

moves.summary: Their words are recast: halakha like him in the large ring, not like him in the others.
moves.about: what Rav and Shmuel meant — halakha like him in the large ring, not like him in the other rings

moves.summary: R׳ Zeira, on reaching Eretz Yisrael, ate meat Rav and Shmuel would have forbidden.
moves.about: R׳ Zeira, on ascending to Eretz Yisrael, ate meat from a slaughter Rav and Shmuel deemed diverted and invalid

moves.cueHe: אמרי ליה: לאו מאתריה דרב ושמואל את?
moves.summary: They challenge him: you come from Rav and Shmuel's own locale.
moves.about: whether he must keep the stringency of Rav and Shmuel, the authorities of the place he came from

moves.summary: He answers that the ruling in their name comes from Yosef bar Ḥiyya, who learns from anyone.
moves.about: who it was that transmitted that ruling in the name of Rav and Shmuel

moves.summary: Rav Yosef, angered, answers that he learned from Rav Yehuda, who transmits even doubtful attributions.
moves.about: whether he learns indiscriminately — he learned from Rav Yehuda, who transmits even uncertainties of attribution

moves.summary: Does R׳ Zeira not hold the rule that a traveller keeps the stringencies of the place he left?
moves.about: whether R׳ Zeira rejects the rule that a traveller takes on the stringencies of the place he left

moves.summary: That rule does not apply to one who ascends from Babylonia to Eretz Yisrael, to whom Babylonia is subordinate.
moves.about: why R׳ Zeira was not bound by the Babylonian stringency once he ascended to Eretz Yisrael

moves.summary: Even granting the rule there, it binds only one who intends to return, and R׳ Zeira did not.
moves.about: why R׳ Zeira was free of the Babylonian stringency — he had no intention of returning

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה אביי לרב יוסף: והא רבנן דאתו ממחוזא
moves.summary: Meḥoza reports R׳ Zeira in Rav Naḥman's name that a diverted cut is valid, against the Babylonian stringency.
moves.about: whether R׳ Zeira himself, in Rav Naḥman's name, held a diverted slaughter valid, against the Babylonian practice Rav Yosef transmits

moves.summary: Each locale follows its own custom, so Meḥoza is no objection.
moves.about: why Meḥoza's practice is no objection — each locale follows its own custom

moves.cueHe: רבי שמעון בן לקיש אכשר בחודא דכובעא
moves.summary: Reish Lakish validates a cut at the tip of the thyroid cartilage.
moves.about: Reish Lakish validated a slaughter cut at the tip of the thyroid cartilage, above the large ring

moves.cueHe: קרי עליה רבי יוחנן: גיסא גיסא
moves.summary: R׳ Yoḥanan derides the ruling as stretching the place of slaughter far too far.
moves.about: mocking Reish Lakish for stretching the bounds of valid slaughter too far

moves.summary: In Rava's name: a cut that encounters the arytenoid cartilage makes the animal a tereifa.
moves.about: that a cut which encounters the arytenoid cartilage renders the animal a tereifa

moves.summary: Does ׳encountered׳ mean touched, as in one verse, or merely reached, as in another?
moves.about: whether ׳encountered׳ in Rava's ruling means touched the arytenoid cartilage or merely reached it without touching

moves.cueHe: איתמר, אמר רב פפא משמיה דרבא
moves.summary: In Rava's name, against Rav Pappi: leaving part of the arytenoid cartilage is valid.
moves.about: that leaving part of the arytenoid cartilage leaves the slaughter valid

moves.cueHe: אמר רב אמימר בר מר ינוקא: הוה קאימנא קמיה
moves.summary: He heard the same ruling standing before R׳ Ḥiyya son of Rav Avya.
moves.about: attending on R׳ Ḥiyya son of Rav Avya and receiving the ruling from him in person

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה רבינא לרב אשי: אמר לי רב שמן מסוברא
moves.summary: A third chain: Mar Zutra taught the same ruling when he visited Suvara.
moves.about: reporting to Rav Ashi what Rav Shemen of Suvara told him about Mar Zutra's teaching

moves.summary: He inverts the ruling: encountering is valid, leaving part makes a tereifa.
moves.about: which case is the valid one — encountering the arytenoid cartilage or leaving part of it

moves.summary: The halakha: from the incline of the thyroid cartilage downward is valid, i.e. like ׳leaving part׳.
moves.about: the halakha follows the view that leaving part of the arytenoid cartilage is valid, i.e. slaughter from the incline of the thyroid cartilage downward

moves.cueHe: רב נחמן אכשר משיפוי כובע ולמטה
moves.summary: Rav Naḥman validated a cut from the incline of the thyroid cartilage downward.
moves.about: Rav Naḥman validated a slaughter from the incline of the thyroid cartilage downward

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה רב חנן בר רב קטינא לרב נחמן: כמאן?
moves.summary: Whose view is that? It matches neither the Rabbis nor R׳ Yosei b׳R׳ Yehuda.
moves.about: which authority Rav Naḥman's ruling follows

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה: אנא לא חילק ידענא
moves.summary: He rules not from either tanna's reasoning but from a tradition with three reported chains.
moves.about: he rules from a received tradition rather than from either tanna's reasoning

moves.cueHe: ואמר רבי יהושע בן לוי: מוגרמת דרבנן
moves.summary: He maps the baraita: what the Rabbis call diverted is valid for R׳ Yosei.
moves.about: that what the Rabbis of the mishna call a diverted slaughter is valid on R׳ Yosei b׳R׳ Yehuda's view

moves.cueHe: ודרבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, כשרה לרבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס
moves.summary: And what R׳ Yosei calls diverted is valid for R׳ Ḥanina ben Antigonus.
moves.about: that what R׳ Yosei b׳R׳ Yehuda calls a diverted slaughter is valid on R׳ Ḥanina ben Antigonus's view

moves.summary: That is obvious from the baraita itself.
moves.about: that R׳ Yehoshua ben Levi's statement is self-evident from the baraita and teaches nothing

moves.summary: Floats the reading that R׳ Ḥanina's testimony addresses only the Rabbis' case.
moves.about: the statement is needed to rule out reading R׳ Ḥanina ben Antigonus as addressing only the Rabbis' case

moves.summary: R׳ Yehoshua ben Levi's statement is needed to rule that reading out.
Re-floats the rejected reading: perhaps it is indeed so.
moves.about: whether a slaughter in which the knife was diverted above the large ring is valid

moves.summary: Were that so the baraita would have said ׳testified about it׳, not the general formula.
moves.about: why not say that R׳ Ḥanina ben Antigonus indeed addressed only the Rabbis' case

moves.summary: The halakha follows R׳ Ḥanina ben Antigonus, as Rav Naḥman ruled like him.
moves.about: if that were so the baraita should have said ׳he testified about it׳ rather than the general ׳about a diverted slaughter׳

moves.cueHe: אמר רב הונא אמר רב אסי: מחלוקת
moves.summary: In Rav Asi's name: the mishna's dispute is only where he cut two-thirds and then diverted.
moves.about: the scope of the mishna's dispute about cutting within the large ring and diverting

moves.cueHe: אבל הגרים שליש, ושחט שני שליש
moves.summary: The reverse order is invalid by all, since a majority must be cut in valid slaughter.
moves.about: confining the mishna's dispute to a case where he cut two-thirds within the ring and then diverted the last third, the reverse order being invalid by all

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה רב חסדא: אדרבה, לימא מר איפכא
moves.summary: The scoping should be inverted: the dispute is where he diverted first.
moves.about: which of the two orders of cutting is the disputed case and which is agreed by all

moves.summary: The Rabbis answer the deficient-windpipe analogy: there the flaw lay in the place of slaughter.
moves.about: the Rabbis distinguish: in the deficient windpipe the flaw was in the place of slaughter, here it is not

moves.cueHe: דהא תנן: רובו של אחד כמוהו
moves.summary: A mishna proves that cutting two-thirds first is valid by all.
moves.about: the mishna that the majority of one siman is like the whole of it

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה רב יוסף: מאן נימא לן
moves.summary: Perhaps that mishna is R׳ Yosei's own teaching, so it proves nothing agreed.
moves.about: whether the mishna ׳the majority of one is like it׳ is agreed by all or is R׳ Yosei b׳R׳ Yehuda's own teaching

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה אביי: אטו כל רובי דעלמא
moves.summary: Are all majority rulings everywhere to be ascribed to R׳ Yosei?
moves.about: whether every ruling that follows a majority is to be ascribed to R׳ Yosei b׳R׳ Yehuda

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה: אנא רובא דשחיטה קאמינא
moves.summary: Only the majority rule in slaughter, where the tannaim are known to disagree.
moves.about: he spoke only of the majority principle in slaughter, where the tannaim are known to disagree

moves.summary: A second version of the whole exchange, with Rav Huna's scoping inverted and the challengers swapped.
moves.about: a second version of the same discussion, with the roles of Rav Ḥisda and Rav Yosef reversed

moves.cueHe: אבל שחט שני שליש, והגרים שליש – דברי הכל כשרה, דהא תנן
moves.summary: In this version it is Rav Huna who proves the agreed case from the mishna of ׳the majority of one׳.
moves.about: the mishna that the majority of one siman is like the whole, proving the reverse order is valid by all

moves.summary: Perhaps that mishna is R׳ Yosei's own teaching.
moves.about: whether the mishna ׳the majority of one is like it׳ may itself be R׳ Yosei b׳R׳ Yehuda's teaching, so it proves nothing agreed

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה רב יוסף: אטו כל רובי דעלמא
moves.summary: Are all majority rulings everywhere his?
moves.about: whether every ruling that follows a majority is to be ascribed to R׳ Yosei b׳R׳ Yehuda

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה: אנא רובא דשחיטה קאמינא
moves.summary: Only the majority rule in slaughter, where they are known to disagree.
moves.about: he spoke only of the majority principle in slaughter, where the tannaim are known to disagree

moves.cueHe: הגרים שליש, ושחט שליש, והגרים שליש – רב הונא אמר רב: כשרה
moves.summary: Two tradents of Rav split on divert-cut-divert: Rav Huna valid, Rav Yehuda a tereifa.
moves.about: that a windpipe cut divert-cut-divert in thirds is valid

moves.cueHe: שחט שליש, והגרים שליש, ושחט שליש – רב יהודה אמר רב: כשרה
moves.summary: In the mirror case Rav Yehuda reports Rav as validating.
moves.about: that a windpipe cut cut-divert-cut in thirds is valid

moves.summary: The same case is put to Rav Huna.
moves.about: whether a windpipe cut cut-divert-cut in thirds is valid

moves.summary: Rav Huna rules it a tereifa, the reverse of Rav Yehuda in both cases.
moves.about: he ruled the animal a tereifa in that case

moves.summary: Rav Yehuda, angered, protests that Rav Huna reverses him in both directions.
moves.about: Rav Yehuda's anger that Rav Huna reverses his rulings in both cases, against what he had heard from Rav

moves.cueHe: אמר רב הונא: שפיר קא מיקפד
moves.summary: Rav Huna concedes: Rav Yehuda heard it from Rav, and a majority was cut in valid slaughter.
moves.about: that Rav Yehuda was right to be angry — he heard the ruling from Rav himself, and a majority was in fact cut by valid slaughter

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה רב חסדא: לא תהדר בך
moves.summary: Do not retract — retracting forfeits your earlier ruling.
moves.about: retracting here would forfeit his earlier ruling, since both turn on where the animal's life left it

moves.summary: The reason you validated there — that life left in valid slaughter — invalidates here.
moves.about: why he validated the first case, where he diverted, cut, and diverted again

moves.cueHe: איקלע רב נחמן לסורא, בעו מיניה
moves.summary: Sura puts the cut-divert-cut case to Rav Naḥman on his visit.
moves.about: whether a windpipe cut cut-divert-cut in thirds is valid

moves.cueHe: אמר להו: לאו היינו דרבי אלעזר בר מניומי
moves.summary: He identifies the case with R׳ Elazar bar Minyumi's comb-like slaughter, which is valid.
moves.about: the case is already settled by R׳ Elazar bar Minyumi's ruling on a comb-like slaughter

moves.summary: Perhaps that ruling covers only a jagged cut wholly inside the place of slaughter.
moves.about: whether R׳ Elazar bar Minyumi spoke only of a jagged cut made entirely within the place of slaughter, so it does not settle this case

moves.summary: Read that way the ruling would be saying nothing at all.
moves.about: if he had spoken of a cut wholly within the place of slaughter his ruling would state nothing worth stating

moves.summary: Floats that we might have required an unbroken, straight slaughter.
moves.about: the ruling is needed lest one require an unbroken, straight slaughter

moves.summary: So the ruling is needed even for a cut wholly in the place of slaughter.
A mnemonic fixing the order of R׳ Abba, Rav Kahana and Rav Yehuda in what follows.
moves.about: a mnemonic (ב-כ-ד) fixing the order of R׳ Abba, Rav Kahana and Rav Yehuda in the coming discussion

moves.cueHe: יתיב רבי אבא אחוריה דרב כהנא
moves.summary: The study-house seating: R׳ Abba behind Rav Kahana, Rav Kahana before Rav Yehuda.
moves.about: R׳ Abba sat behind Rav Kahana while Rav Kahana sat before Rav Yehuda

moves.cueHe: ויתיב וקאמר: שחט שליש והגרים שליש ושחט שליש, מהו?
moves.summary: He asks Rav Yehuda about cut-divert-cut.
moves.about: whether a windpipe cut cut-divert-cut in thirds is valid

moves.summary: Valid.
moves.about: that such a slaughter is valid

moves.cueHe: הגרים שליש ושחט שליש והגרים שליש, מהו?
moves.summary: And divert-cut-divert?
moves.about: whether a windpipe cut divert-cut-divert in thirds is valid

moves.summary: Not valid.
moves.about: that such a slaughter is not valid

moves.summary: And a cut begun at an existing perforation?
moves.about: whether a cut begun at a perforation in the windpipe is valid

moves.summary: Valid.
moves.about: that such a slaughter is valid

moves.summary: And a cut that runs into a perforation partway?
moves.about: whether a cut that runs into a perforation partway through is valid

moves.summary: Not valid.
moves.about: that such a slaughter is not valid

moves.cueHe: אזל רבי אבא, אמרה קמיה דרבי אלעזר
moves.summary: R׳ Abba carries the rulings to R׳ Elazar, who carries them to R׳ Yoḥanan.
moves.about: reciting Rav Yehuda's rulings on interrupted slaughter in R׳ Elazar's presence in Eretz Yisrael

moves.summary: What distinguishes the two perforation cases?
moves.about: what distinguishes a cut begun at a perforation from a cut that runs into one

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה: שחט במקום נקב, נעשה כמי ששחט גוי
moves.summary: The gentile analogy: who begins and who finishes decides validity.
moves.about: the two cases are like a gentile who begins a slaughter and a Jew who finishes it, and the reverse

moves.summary: R׳ Yoḥanan mocks the answer and does not accept it.
moves.about: whether the gentile analogy really distinguishes a cut begun at a perforation from one that runs into a perforation

moves.cueHe: אמר רבא: שפיר קרי עליה ״גוי גוי״
moves.summary: Rava supplies the argument: with one slaughterer throughout, the two perforation cases cannot differ.
moves.about: the gentile case fails only because a Jew did not cut the majority, whereas here one man cut throughout, so beginning at a perforation and running into one cannot differ

edges.cueHe: הלכה כרבי יוסי ברבי יהודה
edges.about: whether the halakha follows R׳ Yosei b׳R׳ Yehuda that cutting the majority of a ring counts as cutting all of it

edges.cueHe: הלכה כרבי יוסי ברבי יהודה
edges.about: whether the halakha follows R׳ Yosei b׳R׳ Yehuda that cutting the majority of a ring counts as cutting all of it

edges.cueHe: רב ושמואל דאמרי תרווייהו
edges.about: both rule that the halakha follows R׳ Yosei b׳R׳ Yehuda but only within the large upper ring

edges.cueHe: לא אמר אלא בטבעת הגדולה ... אבל בשאר טבעות – לא
edges.about: confining R׳ Yosei b׳R׳ Yehuda's leniency to the large upper ring, which alone encircles the whole windpipe

edges.cueHe: לא אמר אלא בטבעת הגדולה ... אבל בשאר טבעות – לא
edges.about: confining R׳ Yosei b׳R׳ Yehuda's leniency to the large upper ring, which alone encircles the whole windpipe

edges.cueHe: ובשאר טבעות לא? והתניא
edges.about: whether R׳ Yosei b׳R׳ Yehuda really withheld his ruling from the rings other than the large one

edges.cueHe: ובשאר טבעות לא? והתניא
edges.about: whether R׳ Yosei b׳R׳ Yehuda really withheld his ruling from the rings other than the large one

edges.cueHe: אזל רבי אלעזר, אמרה קמיה דרבי יוחנן
edges.about: reciting the same rulings in R׳ Yoḥanan's presence

edges.cueHe: אמר ליה: מאי שנא?
edges.about: what distinguishes a cut begun at a perforation from a cut that runs into one

edges.cueHe: אמר ליה: שחט במקום נקב, נעשה כמי ששחט גוי וגמר ישראל
edges.about: the two cases are like a gentile who begins a slaughter and a Jew who finishes it, and the reverse

edges.cueHe: קרי עליה: ״גוי גוי״
edges.about: mocking R׳ Elazar for answering with nothing but the gentile analogy

edges.cueHe: קרי עליה: ״גוי גוי״
edges.about: whether the gentile analogy really distinguishes a cut begun at a perforation from one that runs into a perforation

edges.cueHe: אמר רבא: שפיר קרי עליה ״גוי גוי״
edges.about: that R׳ Yoḥanan was right to dismiss R׳ Elazar's gentile analogy

edges.cueHe: בשלמא התם ... אלא הכא מכדי משחט שחיט
edges.about: the gentile case fails only because a Jew did not cut the majority, whereas here one man cut throughout, so beginning at a perforation and running into one cannot differ

extras.cueHe: רב ושמואל דאמרי תרווייהו
extras.about: both rule that the halakha follows R׳ Yosei b׳R׳ Yehuda but only within the large upper ring

extras.cueHe: ומוגרמת פסולה. העיד רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס על מוגרמת שהיא כשרה
extras.about: whether a slaughter in which the knife was diverted above the ring (מוגרמת) is valid

extras.cueHe: סברי כוותיה בחדא
extras.about: whether cutting the majority of the windpipe within the large ring is a valid slaughter

extras.cueHe: סברי כוותיה בחדא
extras.about: whether cutting the majority of the windpipe within the large ring is a valid slaughter

extras.cueHe: ופליגי עליה בחדא
extras.about: whether slaughter within the rings other than the large upper ring is valid

extras.cueHe: ופליגי עליה בחדא
extras.about: whether slaughter within the rings other than the large upper ring is valid

extras.cueHe: יוסף בר חייא מכולי עלמא גמיר
extras.about: impugning Rav Yosef as a tradent who learns from anyone, so the ruling reported in Rav and Shmuel's name is unreliable

extras.cueHe: אנא מרב יהודה גמירנא
extras.about: the master from whom Rav Yosef received his traditions

extras.cueHe: דאמר רב יהודה
extras.about: an instance of Rav Yehuda's precision: a ruling transmitted with its attribution left in doubt

extras.cueHe: אמר רב יהודה: אמר רבי ירמיה בר אבא
extras.about: a tribunal of three permits a blemished firstborn where there is no expert

extras.cueHe: ספק משמיה דשמואל
extras.about: the ruling on the blemished firstborn, reported uncertainly in Shmuel's name

extras.cueHe: נותנין עליו חומרי המקום שיצא משם וחומרי המקום שהלך לשם
extras.about: the mishna of local customs, imposing on a traveller the stringencies of both places

extras.cueHe: רב אשי אמר: אפילו תימא מבבל לארץ ישראל
extras.about: why R׳ Zeira could abandon the Babylonian stringency on ascending to Eretz Yisrael — Babylonia's subordination, or his not intending to return

extras.cueHe: רבנן דאתו ממחוזא אמרי, אמר רבי זירא
extras.about: reporting R׳ Zeira's ruling, in Rav Naḥman's name, that a diverted slaughter is valid

extras.cueHe: אמר רבי זירא משמיה דרב נחמן
extras.about: that a slaughter in which the knife was diverted above the ring is valid

extras.cueHe: גיסא גיסא
extras.about: whether a cut at the tip of the thyroid cartilage still lies within the place of slaughter

extras.cueHe: דכתיב ״ויפגע בו וימת״
extras.about: scriptural evidence that פגע can mean actual contact

extras.cueHe: כדכתיב ״ויפגעו בו מלאכי אלהים״
extras.about: scriptural evidence that פגע can mean an encounter without contact

extras.cueHe: איתמר, אמר רב פפא משמיה דרבא
extras.about: the transmitted ruling that leaving part of the arytenoid cartilage is valid

extras.cueHe: שייר בחיטי – כשרה
extras.about: which handling of the arytenoid cartilage invalidates the slaughter — encountering it or leaving part of it — both reported in Rava's name

extras.cueHe: ואמר לי: שייר בחיטי – כשרה
extras.about: that leaving part of the arytenoid cartilage leaves the slaughter valid

extras.cueHe: איקלע מר זוטרא לאתרין ודרש
extras.about: Mar Zutra's public teaching that leaving part of the arytenoid cartilage leaves the slaughter valid

extras.cueHe: דאמר רבי חייא בר אבא
extras.about: the received ruling that slaughter from the incline of the thyroid cartilage downward is valid

extras.cueHe: אמר רבי חייא בר אבא אמר רבי יוחנן
extras.about: that slaughter from the incline of the thyroid cartilage downward is valid

extras.cueHe: ואמרי לה אמר רבי יעקב בר אידי אמר רבי יהושע בן לוי
extras.about: the same ruling, in a third alternative chain of transmission

extras.cueHe: דקאי רב נחמן כוותיה
extras.about: whether slaughter from the incline of the thyroid cartilage downward, beyond the large ring, is valid

extras.cueHe: דרבנן סברי: כולה שחיטה בעינן בטבעת גדולה
extras.about: the Rabbis require the whole slaughter to be performed within the large ring

extras.cueHe: ורבי יוסי ברבי יהודה סבר: רובו ככולו
extras.about: R׳ Yosei b׳R׳ Yehuda holds that the majority is like the whole

extras.cueHe: דרבנן סברי ... ורבי יוסי ברבי יהודה סבר
extras.about: whether cutting two-thirds of the windpipe within the large ring and diverting the last third is a valid slaughter

extras.cueHe: דרבי יוסי ברבי יהודה סבר מידי דהוה אחצי קנה פגום
extras.about: R׳ Yosei b׳R׳ Yehuda validates a cut begun with diversion, as with a windpipe already half deficient

extras.cueHe: אמר רב הונא אמר רב אסי
extras.about: in the alternative version, that the dispute concerns diverting first and then cutting two-thirds

extras.cueHe: רב יהודה אמר רב: טרפה
extras.about: that a windpipe cut divert-cut-divert in thirds is a tereifa

extras.cueHe: רב הונא אמר רב: כשרה, רב יהודה אמר רב: טרפה
extras.about: whether a windpipe cut divert-cut-divert in thirds is valid, and what Rav ruled about it

extras.cueHe: דאמר רבי אלעזר בר מניומי: שחיטה העשויה כמסרק כשרה
extras.about: that a slaughter performed like the teeth of a comb is valid
